title: Suffix 面: 前面, 里面, 上面
explanation: 面 after a direction word makes a place word, just like 边: 前面, 后面, 里面, 外面, 上面, 下面. Most of the time 面 and 边 mean the same thing here. Like other place words, they go after the noun: 书包里面.
pattern: Noun + 前面/后面/里面/外面/上面/下面

examples.py: Shūbāo lǐmiàn yǒu shénme?
examples.en: What's in the schoolbag?

examples.py: Wǒ jiā hòumiàn yǒu yí gè shāngchǎng.
examples.en: There's a shopping mall behind my home.

title: Left and right: 左 and 右
explanation: 左 is left and 右 is right. As place words they usually take 边: 左边, 右边. When giving directions, people often say 往左 or 往右 before a verb.
pattern: 在 + 左边/右边, 往 + 左/右 + Verb

examples.py: Xǐshǒujiān zài zuǒbian.
examples.en: The toilet is on the left.

examples.py: Nǐ wǎng yòu zǒu jiù dào le.
examples.en: Go right and you'll be there.

title: Doubling verbs: 看看, 看一看, 休息休息
explanation: Saying a verb twice makes it sound short and relaxed, like 'have a look' or 'take a little rest'. One-syllable verbs become AA or A一A (看看, 看一看), and for something already done you use A了A (看了看). Two-syllable verbs become ABAB (休息休息), never AABB.

examples.py: Wǒmen xiūxi xiūxi ba.
examples.en: Let's take a little break.

examples.py: Tā kàn le kàn shǒubiǎo.
examples.en: He glanced at his watch.

title: Maybe, probably: 可能
explanation: 可能 before a verb means 'may' or 'probably'. It can also go at the very start of the sentence: 可能他不来了. 不可能 means 'that can't be' or 'there's no way'.

examples.py: Míngtiān kěnéng xià yǔ.
examples.en: It might rain tomorrow.

examples.py: Tā kěnéng bù zhīdào.
examples.en: He probably doesn't know.

title: Separable verbs: 帮忙, 游泳, 跳舞, 跑步
explanation: 帮忙 is really 帮 + 忙, so it can't take an object after it. Say 帮我 or 帮我一个忙, not 帮忙我. The same goes for 游泳, 跳舞 and 跑步: other words can go in the middle, but no object can come after.

examples.py: Nǐ néng bāng wǒ yí gè máng ma?
examples.en: Can you do me a favour?

examples.py: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang pǎobù.
examples.en: I go running every morning.

title: Why: 为什么
explanation: 为什么 asks why. It usually goes after the subject and before the verb, not at the start like English. You answer with 因为.

examples.py: Nǐ wèishénme bú qù?
examples.en: Why aren't you going?

examples.py: Tā wèishénme méiyǒu lái shàngkè?
examples.en: Why didn't he come to class?

title: Oneself: 自己
explanation: 自己 means oneself. It can follow a pronoun to stress who did it (我自己), or go before a verb to mean 'by yourself, on your own'.

examples.py: Zhè shì wǒ zìjǐ zuò de fàn.
examples.en: I made this food myself.

examples.py: Tā xiǎng zìjǐ qù.
examples.en: He wants to go on his own.

title: So, like this, every: 这么, 那么, 这样, 那样, 每
explanation: 这么 and 那么 before an adjective mean 'so': 这么冷. 这样 and 那样 mean 'like this' and 'like that'. 每 means every and needs a measure word or time word after it, like 每天, often with 都 later in the sentence.
pattern: 这么/那么 + adjective, 每 + measure word/time word

examples.py: Jīntiān zěnme zhème lěng?
examples.en: Why is it so cold today?

examples.py: Wǒ měitiān dōu hē chá.
examples.en: I drink tea every day.

title: Doubling adjectives: 慢慢, 高高兴兴
explanation: Saying an adjective twice makes it more vivid. One-syllable adjectives become AA (慢慢), and two-syllable ones become AABB (高高兴兴). Don't put 很 before a doubled adjective.

examples.py: Nǐ mànmàn shuō.
examples.en: Take your time and say it slowly.

examples.zh: 我们高高兴兴地去旅游了。
examples.py: Wǒmen gāogāoxìngxìng de qù lǚyóu le.
examples.en: We went off on our trip in high spirits.

title: Big numbers and 'lots': 万, 好多, 多
explanation: 万 is ten thousand, so 一万 is 10,000 and 十万 is 100,000. 好多 means a lot of, like 很多 but more spoken. 多 can also follow a round number to mean 'more than', as in 一万多.

examples.py: Zhège diànnǎo yí wàn duō kuài.
examples.en: This computer costs over ten thousand yuan.

examples.py: Jīntiān lái le hǎoduō rén.
examples.en: Lots of people came today.

title: Measure words: 条, 位, 间, 名
explanation: 条 is for long, thin things like roads, fish and trousers. 位 is a polite measure word for people, 间 is for rooms, and 名 is for people in a formal count, like students.

examples.py: Zhè tiáo lù hěn cháng.
examples.en: This road is long.

examples.py: Nà wèi shì wǒmen de xīn lǎoshī.
examples.en: That's our new teacher.

title: Containers as measure words: 包
explanation: 包 means bag or packet, and it can be a measure word for things that come in one. 一包牛奶 is a packet of milk. The number goes before 包 and the thing after it.

examples.py: Tā měitiān hē yì bāo niúnǎi.
examples.en: He drinks a packet of milk every day.

examples.py: Wǒ gěi nǐ yì bāo shuǐguǒ.
examples.en: Here's a bag of fruit for you.

title: Times: 次
explanation: 次 counts how many times something happens. Put number + 次 after the verb. A place can go before or after the count, but a pronoun like 他 goes before it: 我见过他一次.

examples.py: Wǒ qù guo Zhōngguó liǎng cì.
examples.en: I've been to China twice.

examples.py: Zhège diànyǐng wǒ kàn le sān cì.
examples.en: I've seen this movie three times.

title: Most, so, how: 最, 好, 多
explanation: 最 means most: 最喜欢 is like best. 好 before an adjective means 'so' or 'really', with feeling: 好冷啊. 多 in an exclamation means 'how': 多漂亮啊.
pattern: 最 + Verb/adjective, 好/多 + adjective + 啊

examples.py: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
examples.en: Football is my favourite thing to play.

examples.py: Jīntiān hǎo lěng a!
examples.en: It's so cold today!

title: Together: 一起
explanation: 一起 means together. It goes before the verb, and the people come before it, often with 和 or 跟: 我和你一起去.
pattern: A + 和/跟 + B + 一起 + Verb

examples.py: Wǒmen yìqǐ qù ba.
examples.en: Let's go together.

examples.py: Wǒ gēn péngyou yìqǐ qù lǚyóu.
examples.en: I'm going on a trip with a friend.

point: 还2、已经、有时（候）、快、快要、正
title: Time adverbs: 已经, 还, 快要, 有时, 正
explanation: 已经 means already and usually comes with 了. 还 means still, 快 or 快要 + verb + 了 means 'about to', and 有时 or 有时候 means sometimes. 正 is like 正在: right at that moment.
pattern: Subject + 已经/还/有时/正 + Verb

examples.zh: 已经十点了，他还在睡觉。
examples.py: Yǐjīng shí diǎn le, tā hái zài shuìjiào.
examples.en: It's already ten, and he's still asleep.

examples.py: Wǒ yǒushí zuò dìtiě qù shàngbān.
examples.en: Sometimes I take the subway to work.

title: Often: 常 and 经常
explanation: 常 and 经常 both mean often and go before the verb. To say 'not often', people usually say 不常.

examples.py: Wǒ jīngcháng qù nàge fànguǎn.
examples.en: I often go to that restaurant.

examples.py: Tā bù cháng hē kāfēi.
examples.en: He doesn't drink coffee much.

title: Don't: 别
explanation: 别 means don't and goes right before the verb. It's like 不要 but more casual. 别……了 means 'stop doing it'.

examples.py: Bié shuì le, kuài qǐchuáng ba!
examples.en: Stop sleeping and get up!

examples.zh: 你别走，我们一起吃饭吧。
examples.py: Nǐ bié zǒu, wǒmen yìqǐ chīfàn ba.
examples.en: Don't go, let's eat together.

title: Then: 再 and 就
explanation: 再 here means 'and then', for something you'll do after another thing: 吃了饭再去. 就 means one thing follows right after another, with no delay: 吃了饭就去. The difference is that 再 suggests waiting until later and 就 suggests straight away.

examples.py: Wǒmen chī le fàn zài qù ba.
examples.en: Let's go after we've eaten.

examples.py: Wǒ xià le bān jiù huí jiā.
examples.en: I go home right after work.

title: Mood adverbs: 都, 就, 还是
explanation: 都 can mean 'already', with a feeling that it's late: 都十二点了. 就 can stress 'right' or 'exactly': 就在前面. 还是 can mean 'had better', as in 你还是去吧.

examples.zh: 都十二点了，你还不睡觉？
examples.py: Dōu shí'èr diǎn le, nǐ hái bú shuìjiào?
examples.en: It's already twelve, and you're still not in bed?

examples.py: Wǒ jiā jiù zài qiánmiàn.
examples.en: My home is just up ahead.

title: From: 从 + time or place
explanation: 从 + time or place shows where or when something starts. It often pairs with 到: 从八点到十二点. The whole phrase goes before the verb.
pattern: 从 + time/place (+ 到 + time/place) + Verb

examples.zh: 我从八点到十二点上课。
examples.py: Wǒ cóng bā diǎn dào shí'èr diǎn shàngkè.
examples.en: I have class from eight to twelve.

examples.py: Tā cóng yīyuàn huílái le.
examples.en: He's back from the hospital.

title: Toward: 往
explanation: 往 + direction or place means toward. It goes before the verb: 往前走, 往左看.

examples.py: Wǎng qián zǒu, jiù dào chēzhàn le.
examples.en: Go straight ahead and you'll reach the station.

examples.py: Nǐ wǎng zuǒbian kàn.
examples.en: Look to your left.

title: Through, by way of: 从
explanation: 从 can also mark the route you take, meaning 'through' or 'by way of': 从这条路走. It still goes before the verb.

examples.py: Wǒmen cóng zhè tiáo lù zǒu ba.
examples.en: Let's go this way.

examples.py: Tā cóng ménkǒu jìnlái le.
examples.en: He came in through the door.

title: For, to: 给 + person + verb
explanation: 给 + person before a verb means doing something for or to that person: 给妈妈打电话. This is different from 给 as a main verb, which means give.

examples.py: Wǒ wǎnshang gěi māma dǎ diànhuà.
examples.en: I'll call Mum tonight.

examples.zh: 他给我介绍了一个朋友。
examples.py: Tā gěi wǒ jièshào le yí gè péngyou.
examples.en: He introduced a friend to me.

title: Than: 比
explanation: A 比 B + adjective means A is more ... than B. Don't put 很 or 非常 before the adjective: say 他比我高, not 他比我很高.

examples.py: Tā bǐ wǒ gāo.
examples.en: He's taller than me.

examples.py: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng.
examples.en: Today is colder than yesterday.

title: With: 跟 + person
explanation: 跟 + person means 'with' and works like 和: 我跟他一起去. With 说 it means telling someone: 跟老师说.

examples.py: Wǒ gēn māma yìqǐ qù shāngchǎng.
examples.en: I'm going to the mall with Mum.

examples.py: Nǐ gēn lǎoshī shuō yíxià ba.
examples.en: Why don't you tell the teacher.

title: Because of: 因为
explanation: 因为 + a short reason can go between the subject and the verb, meaning 'because of': 他因为生病没有来. The result follows right after.

examples.zh: 他因为生病没有来上课。
examples.py: Tā yīnwèi shēngbìng méiyǒu lái shàngkè.
examples.en: He didn't come to class because he was sick.

examples.py: Wǒ yīnwèi xià yǔ méiyǒu chūmén.
examples.en: I didn't go out because of the rain.

title: And: 跟
explanation: 跟 can join two nouns or pronouns, just like 和: 我跟他. Like 和, it doesn't join two whole sentences.

examples.py: Wǒ gēn tā dōu shì xuésheng.
examples.en: He and I are both students.

examples.py: Wǒ mǎi le bǐ gēn běnzi.
examples.en: I bought pens and notebooks.

point: 但、但是、那、虽然、还是2、因为2、所以
title: Linking clauses: 但是, 虽然, 因为, 所以, 那, 还是
explanation: 但是 or 但 means but, 虽然 means although, 因为 means because and 所以 means so. 那 at the start of a reply means 'then, in that case', and 还是 in a question means 'or'. Chinese often uses them in pairs, like 虽然……但是…….

examples.py: Wǒ xiǎng qù, dànshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
examples.en: I want to go, but I don't have time.

examples.zh: 你不想去？那我自己去吧。
examples.py: Nǐ bù xiǎng qù? Nà wǒ zìjǐ qù ba.
examples.en: You don't want to go? Then I'll go by myself.

title: The particles 得 and 地
explanation: 得 comes after a verb to say how well or in what way it's done: 说得很好. 地 comes after a describing word and before a verb: 高兴地笑了. 的, 得 and 地 are all said de, so watch the character.
pattern: Verb + 得 + adjective, adjective + 地 + Verb

examples.py: Tā Hànyǔ shuō de hěn hǎo.
examples.en: He speaks Chinese really well.

examples.py: Tā gāoxìng de xiào le.
examples.en: She smiled happily.

title: Have done before: 过
explanation: 过 after a verb means you've done it at some time before. The negative is 没有 + verb + 过, and you keep 过 in the negative.

examples.py: Wǒ chī guo jiǎozi.
examples.en: I've had dumplings before.

examples.py: Wǒ méiyǒu zuò guo fēijī.
examples.en: I've never been on a plane.

title: Ongoing state: 着
explanation: 着 after a verb shows that a state is going on: 拿着 means holding, 开着 means open. It's about how things are, while 在 + verb is about an action happening.

examples.py: Tā shǒu li ná zhe yì běn shū.
examples.en: He's holding a book.

examples.py: Mén kāi zhe, nǐ jìnlái ba.
examples.en: The door's open, come on in.

title: More sentence-end particles: 呢, 吧, 的, 啊
explanation: 吧 can show you're guessing and want the other person to confirm: 你是老师吧？ 呢 can add stress to a statement, 的 makes it sound sure, and 啊 adds warm feeling to it.

examples.py: Nǐ shì Zhōngguó rén ba?
examples.en: You're Chinese, right?

examples.py: Zhèlǐ zhēn piàoliang a!
examples.en: It's so beautiful here!

title: Verb + complement phrases
explanation: A verb can take a word right after it that shows the result or direction of the action: 听懂, 写完, 走进来. This word is the complement.

examples.py: Wǒ tīng dǒng le.
examples.en: I understood.

examples.py: Nǐ kàn dǒng zhè běn shū le ma?
examples.en: Did you understand this book?

title: 的 phrases: the red one, mine
explanation: A word or phrase + 的 can stand for a noun you already know: 红色的 means the red one, 我的 means mine. 吃的 means things to eat.

examples.py: Zhège shì wǒ de.
examples.en: This one is mine.

examples.py: Wǒ yào hóngsè de.
examples.en: I want the red one.

title: Two verb phrases in a row
explanation: Two verb phrases with the same subject can follow each other with no linking word: 坐地铁去机场. The first often shows how or where, and the second what you do or why.

examples.py: Wǒmen zuò dìtiě qù jīchǎng.
examples.en: We're taking the subway to the airport.

examples.py: Tā qù fànguǎn chīfàn le.
examples.en: He went to a restaurant to eat.

title: Ask or let someone do something
explanation: In 请/让/叫 + person + verb, the person is the object of the first verb and the doer of the second. That's how you say 'ask, let or tell someone to do something': 让他来.

examples.py: Māma ràng wǒ qù mǎi niúnǎi.
examples.en: Mum told me to go and buy milk.

examples.py: Wǒ qǐng nǐ chīfàn.
examples.en: Let me treat you to a meal.

title: Noun phrases
explanation: A noun phrase works like a noun. It has a noun at its center with describing words before it, like 我的好朋友. It can be the subject or the object.

examples.zh: 我的好朋友在中国工作。
examples.py: Wǒ de hǎo péngyou zài Zhōngguó gōngzuò.
examples.en: My good friend works in China.

examples.zh: 我喜欢那个白色的书包。
examples.py: Wǒ xǐhuan nàge báisè de shūbāo.
examples.en: I like that white schoolbag.

title: Verb phrases
explanation: A verb phrase has a verb at its center, plus words before it or objects after it: 经常跑步, 去外国旅游. It works like a verb in the sentence.

examples.py: Tā jīngcháng pǎobù.
examples.en: He runs a lot.

examples.py: Wǒ xiǎng qù wàiguó lǚyóu.
examples.en: I'd like to travel abroad.

title: Adjective phrases
explanation: An adjective phrase has an adjective at its center, often with a degree word before it: 很累, 非常舒服. It works like an adjective in the sentence.

examples.py: Jīntiān wǒ hěn lèi.
examples.en: I'm really tired today.

examples.py: Zhège fángjiān fēicháng shūfu.
examples.en: This room is really comfortable.

title: And so on: 什么的
explanation: 什么的 goes at the end of a list to mean 'and so on' or 'that kind of thing'. It's casual and spoken.

examples.zh: 我买了苹果、牛奶什么的。
examples.py: Wǒ mǎi le píngguǒ, niúnǎi shénmede.
examples.en: I bought apples, milk, that kind of thing.

examples.zh: 他喜欢跑步、游泳什么的。
examples.py: Tā xǐhuan pǎobù, yóuyǒng shénmede.
examples.en: He likes running, swimming and so on.

title: You'd better: 还是……吧
explanation: 还是……吧 suggests what you think is the better choice, like 'you'd better' or 'let's just'. It usually comes after thinking about the options.

examples.zh: 下雨了，我们还是打车去吧。
examples.py: Xià yǔ le, wǒmen háishi dǎchē qù ba.
examples.en: It's raining, let's just take a taxi.

examples.zh: 你生病了，还是在家休息吧。
examples.py: Nǐ shēngbìng le, háishi zài jiā xiūxi ba.
examples.en: You're sick, you'd better rest at home.

title: About to: 要/快要/就要……了
explanation: These mean something is about to happen, and 了 goes at the end. 快要 stresses that it's very soon. If there's a time word like 明天, use 就要, not 快要: 明天就要考试了.
pattern: (Time) + 要/快要/就要 + Verb + 了

examples.py: Huǒchē kuàiyào kāi le.
examples.en: The train's about to leave.

examples.py: Wǒmen míngtiān jiù yào kǎoshì le.
examples.en: We have an exam tomorrow.

title: Already: 都……了
explanation: 都……了 means 'already', with a feeling that it's late or that it's a lot. It's often followed by a push to do something.

examples.py: Dōu bā diǎn le, kuài qǐchuáng ba!
examples.en: It's already eight, get up!

examples.zh: 我们都等了一个小时了。
examples.py: Wǒmen dōu děng le yí gè xiǎoshí le.
examples.en: We've already been waiting for an hour.

title: The thing done as the subject
explanation: The thing an action is done to can go first, with no word for 'by': 饭做好了 means the meal is ready. This is very common when it doesn't matter who did it.

examples.py: Fàn zuò hǎo le.
examples.en: The food's ready.

examples.py: Yīfu xǐ wán le.
examples.en: The clothes have been washed.

title: Noun phrases as the predicate
explanation: For ages, prices and dates, a noun phrase can follow the subject directly without 是: 我妹妹十八岁. For the negative you need 不是.

examples.py: Wǒ mèimei shíbā suì.
examples.en: My younger sister is eighteen.

examples.py: Zhè jiàn yīfu sānbǎi kuài.
examples.en: This piece of clothing is three hundred yuan.

point: 动词或动词性短语、主谓短语作定语
title: Verb phrases that describe a noun
explanation: A verb phrase or a small subject + verb can describe a noun, with 的 before the noun: 我买的书 is the book I bought. The describing part always comes first, unlike English 'the book that I bought'.
pattern: Verb phrase / subject + verb + 的 + Noun

examples.py: Zhè shì wǒ zuótiān mǎi de shū.
examples.en: This is the book I bought yesterday.

examples.py: Wǒ xǐhuan nǐ zuò de cài.
examples.en: I like the food you cook.

title: Result complements: 错, 懂, 好, 会, 完
explanation: Put 错, 懂, 好, 会 or 完 right after a verb to show the result: 写错 is write wrongly, 听懂 is understand, 做好 is get done, 学会 is learn how, 吃完 is finish eating. The negative is 没有 + verb + result: 我没有听懂.

examples.py: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ xiě cuò le.
examples.en: Sorry, I wrote it wrong.

examples.py: Nǐ chī wán le ma?
examples.en: Have you finished eating?

point: 简单趋向补语的趋向意义用法：（1）动词+来/去
title: Direction: verb + 来/去
explanation: 来 after a verb means toward the speaker, and 去 means away from the speaker: 进来 is come in, 回去 is go back. A place goes before 来 or 去: 回家去.

examples.py: Nǐmen jìnlái ba.
examples.en: Come on in.

examples.py: Tā huí jiā qù le.
examples.en: He's gone home.

title: Direction: verb + 上, 下, 进, 出, 过, 回
explanation: These words after a verb show which way something moves: 走进 is walk into, 拿出 is take out, 跑回 is run back. A place or thing usually follows: 走进教室.
pattern: Verb + 上/下/进/出/过/回 + place/thing

examples.py: Tā zǒu jìn jiàoshì.
examples.en: He walked into the classroom.

examples.py: Wǒ ná chū yì běn shū kàn le kàn.
examples.en: I took out a book and had a look at it.

point: 复合趋向补语的趋向意义用法：动词+出来/出去/过来/过去/回来/回去/进来/进去/起来/上来/上去/下来/下去
title: Two-part directions: 出来, 回去, 起来
explanation: Join 上, 下, 进, 出, 回, 过 or 起 with 来 or 去 for a two-part direction: 走出来, 跑回去, 站起来. A place goes between the two parts: 走进教室来.
pattern: Verb + 上/下/进/出/回/过/起 + 来/去

examples.py: Tā cóng fángjiān li zǒu chūlái le.
examples.en: He walked out of the room.

examples.py: Lǎoshī lái le, dàjiā zhàn qǐlái.
examples.en: The teacher's here, everyone stand up.

title: How it's done: verb + 得 + adjective
explanation: Verb + 得 + adjective phrase describes how an action is done: 跑得很快. If there's an object, put it before the verb or say the verb twice: 他汉语说得很好, or 他说汉语说得很好.

examples.py: Tā pǎo de hěn kuài.
examples.en: He runs fast.

examples.py: Nǐ jīntiān lái de hěn zǎo.
examples.en: You came early today.

title: How long: verb + time
explanation: To say how long an action lasts, put the length of time after the verb: 等了一个小时. With an object, the time usually goes between the verb and the object: 学了两年汉语.

examples.py: Wǒ xué le liǎng nián Hànyǔ.
examples.en: I studied Chinese for two years.

examples.py: Tā děng le nǐ yí gè xiǎoshí.
examples.en: He waited an hour for you.

title: By how much: adjective + amount
explanation: After an adjective, an amount can say by how much: 大两岁, 长一点儿. You'll see this a lot with 比, but it also works on its own.

examples.py: Wǒ gēge dà wǒ liǎng suì.
examples.en: My older brother is two years older than me.

examples.py: Zhè tiáo kùzi cháng le yìdiǎnr.
examples.en: These trousers are a bit too long.

title: Topic + subject + predicate
explanation: The predicate can itself be a little subject + predicate: 他个子很高 means he is tall. The first part is the topic, and the second subject is a part or feature of it.

examples.py: Tā gèzi hěn gāo.
examples.en: He's tall.

examples.py: Wǒ jīntiān tóu hěn téng.
examples.en: I have a bad headache today.

point: 用“还是”连接的选择问句
title: Either-or questions with 还是
explanation: A 还是 B？ asks which of two choices: 你喝茶还是喝咖啡？ Don't add 吗. In a statement, 'or' is 或者, not 还是.

examples.py: Nǐ hē chá háishi hē kāfēi?
examples.en: Would you like tea or coffee?

examples.py: Nǐ jīntiān qù háishi míngtiān qù?
examples.en: Are you going today or tomorrow?

title: Don't do that: 别 commands
explanation: 别 + verb tells someone not to do something. Add 了 at the end to mean 'stop doing it' or 'don't bother'.

examples.py: Bié wán shǒujī le.
examples.en: Put your phone away.

examples.py: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, bié chūqù le.
examples.en: It's cold out, don't go outside.

title: 是 to describe or explain
explanation: 是 can also explain what something is like or what kind it is, not just that A equals B. You'll often see 的 at the end: 我的手机是白色的.

examples.py: Tā shì yí gè hěn hǎo de lǎoshī.
examples.en: He's a really good teacher.

examples.py: Wǒ de shǒujī shì báisè de.
examples.en: My phone is white.

title: 有 for reaching an amount
explanation: 有 + amount can mean that something reaches that amount: 有六岁 is about six years old. It's common in questions with 多: 有多远？ means how far is it.
pattern: Subject + 有 + amount / 有多 + adjective？

examples.py: Zhège háizi yǒu liù suì le ba?
examples.en: This kid must be about six, right?

examples.py: Cóng zhèr dào jīchǎng yǒu duō yuǎn?
examples.en: How far is it from here to the airport?

point: 处所+动词+着(+数量短语)+名词
title: What's at a place: place + verb + 着 + noun
explanation: Place + verb + 着 + noun describes what is at a place and in what state: 门口站着一个孩子. The place comes first and the person or thing comes last.
pattern: Place + Verb + 着 + (number + measure word) + Noun

examples.py: Ménkǒu zhàn zhe yí gè háizi.
examples.en: There's a child standing at the door.

examples.py: Yǐzi shang zuò zhe yí wèi lǎoshī.
examples.en: A teacher is sitting on the chair.

title: A 比 B + adjective
explanation: A 比 B + adjective means A is more ... than B. The adjective stays bare, with no 很 before it. To say A isn't more ... than B, use 没有 instead of 不比.

examples.py: Zuò dìtiě bǐ dǎchē piányi.
examples.en: The subway is cheaper than a taxi.

examples.py: Zhège fángjiān bǐ nàge dà.
examples.en: This room is bigger than that one.

point: （2）A比B+形容词+数量补语/程度补语
title: A 比 B + adjective + how much
explanation: Add an amount after the adjective to say how much more: 贵十块. Use 多了 for 'much more' and 一点儿 for 'a bit more'. Don't use 很 or 非常 in this pattern.
pattern: A + 比 + B + adjective + amount/多了/一点儿

examples.py: Zhège bǐ nàge guì shí kuài.
examples.en: This one is ten yuan more than that one.

examples.py: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng duō le.
examples.en: Today is much colder than yesterday.

title: As ... as: A 有/没有 B + adjective
explanation: A 有 B + adjective means A is as ... as B, and A 没有 B + adjective means A isn't as ... as B. You can add 这么 or 那么 before the adjective.
pattern: A + 有/没有 + B + (这么/那么) + adjective

examples.py: Wǒ méiyǒu tā nàme gāo.
examples.en: I'm not as tall as him.

examples.py: Nǐ mèimei yǒu nǐ zhème gāo ma?
examples.en: Is your sister as tall as you?

point: （4）A比B+动词+得+形容词/A+动词+得+比+B+形容词
title: Comparing actions with 比 and 得
explanation: To compare how two people do something, put 比 B before the verb or after 得: 他比我跑得快 or 他跑得比我快. Both mean he runs faster than me.
pattern: A + 比 + B + Verb + 得 + adjective / A + Verb + 得 + 比 + B + adjective

examples.py: Tā bǐ wǒ pǎo de kuài.
examples.en: He runs faster than me.

examples.py: Wǒ mèimei chàng de bǐ wǒ hǎo.
examples.en: My younger sister sings better than me.

point: 强调时间、地点、方式、动作者
title: 是……的 to stress when, where, how or who
explanation: Use 是……的 to stress the time, place, way or person for something that already happened: 我是坐飞机来的. 是 goes right before the part you're stressing, and in speech it's often dropped.
pattern: Subject + 是 + when/where/how + Verb + 的

examples.py: Wǒ shì zuótiān lái de.
examples.en: I came yesterday.

examples.py: Nǐ shì zěnme lái de?
examples.en: How did you get here?

point: 表使令：主语+请/叫/让……+宾语1+动词+宾语2
title: Asking or telling someone: 请/叫/让
explanation: Subject + 请/叫/让 + person + verb means asking, telling or letting someone do something. 请 is polite, while 叫 and 让 are more direct.
pattern: Subject + 请/叫/让 + person + Verb + Object

examples.py: Lǎoshī ràng wǒmen xiě Hànzì.
examples.en: The teacher had us write characters.

examples.py: Māma jiào wǒ huí jiā chīfàn.
examples.en: Mum called me home for dinner.

title: Verb + 给 + person + thing
explanation: Verbs like 送 and 拿 can take 给 to show who gets the thing: 送给她一件衣服. The person comes right after 给, then the thing.

examples.py: Wǒ sòng gěi tā yí jiàn yīfu.
examples.en: I gave her a piece of clothing as a present.

examples.py: Qǐng ná gěi wǒ nà běn shū.
examples.en: Please pass me that book.

title: (是)……，还是……: this or that?
explanation: This pattern gives two choices in a question: (是) A，还是 B？ The 是 at the start is optional. Don't end it with 吗.

examples.zh: 你是坐地铁去，还是打车去？
examples.py: Nǐ shì zuò dìtiě qù, háishi dǎchē qù?
examples.en: Are you taking the subway or a taxi?

examples.py: Shì nǐ qù, háishi wǒ qù?
examples.en: Are you going, or am I?

title: Although ..., but ...: 虽然……，但是……
explanation: 虽然 goes in the first clause and 但是 in the second. English uses only one of 'although' or 'but', but Chinese usually uses both. 还是 after 但是 means 'still'.

examples.zh: 虽然很累，但是我很高兴。
examples.py: Suīrán hěn lèi, dànshì wǒ hěn gāoxìng.
examples.en: I'm tired, but I'm happy.

examples.zh: 虽然下雨了，但是他还是来了。
examples.py: Suīrán xià yǔ le, dànshì tā háishi lái le.
examples.en: It rained, but he still came.

title: Because ..., so ...: 因为……，所以……
explanation: 因为 gives the reason in the first clause and 所以 gives the result in the second. Chinese is happy to use both together, which English doesn't do.

examples.zh: 因为下雨，所以我没有出门。
examples.py: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ méiyǒu chūmén.
examples.en: It was raining, so I didn't go out.

examples.zh: 因为他生病了，所以没有来上课。
examples.py: Yīnwèi tā shēngbìng le, suǒyǐ méiyǒu lái shàngkè.
examples.en: He was sick, so he didn't come to class.

title: As soon as: 一……就……
explanation: 一 + action 1, 就 + action 2 means the second thing happens as soon as the first one does. Both 一 and 就 go before their verbs, after the subject.
pattern: Subject + 一 + Verb 1 + 就 + Verb 2

examples.py: Wǒ yì huí jiā jiù shuìjiào le.
examples.en: I went to bed as soon as I got home.

examples.py: Tā yí kàn jiù dǒng le.
examples.en: He got it the moment he saw it.

point: 动词+着：（1）表示状态的持续
title: Verb + 着 for a lasting state
explanation: 着 after a verb shows a state that stays the same: 坐着 is sitting, 开着 is open. The negative is 没有 + verb + 着.

examples.py: Jiàoshì de mén kāi zhe.
examples.en: The classroom door is open.

examples.py: Tā zài yǐzi shang zuò zhe.
examples.en: He's sitting on the chair.

title: Verb + 着 while doing something else
explanation: 着 can also show an action going on in the background while you do something else: 笑着说 is to say with a smile. The 着 verb comes first, then the main action.

examples.py: Tā xiào zhe shuō: “Méishì.”
examples.en: He said with a smile, "It's fine."

examples.py: Wǒmen zǒu zhe qù ba.
examples.en: Let's walk there.

title: Experience with 过
explanation: Verb + 过 says you've had the experience at some point. To ask, add 吗 or 没有 at the end: 你去过吗？ 你去过没有？

examples.py: Nǐ qù guo nàge fànguǎn ma?
examples.en: Have you been to that restaurant?

examples.py: Wǒ xué guo yìdiǎnr Hànyǔ.
examples.en: I've studied a little Chinese.

title: Order without 第: 五楼
explanation: A number + measure word can show order without 第, especially for floors and rooms: 五楼 is the fifth floor. Context tells you it means 'number five', not 'five floors'.

examples.py: Wǒ jiā zài wǔ lóu.
examples.en: I live on the fifth floor.

examples.py: Wǒmen de jiàoshì zài sān lóu.
examples.en: Our classroom is on the third floor.

point: 概数表达法1：（1）用“几”表示概数
title: A few: 几 in statements
explanation: In a statement, 几 means 'a few' or 'several': 几本书. 十几 means a bit over ten, and 几十 means a few dozen.
pattern: 几 + measure word + noun, 十几/几十 + measure word

examples.py: Wǒ mǎi le jǐ běn shū.
examples.en: I bought a few books.

examples.py: Jiàoshì li yǒu shíjǐ gè xuésheng.
examples.en: There are a dozen or so students in the classroom.

title: More than: number + 多 + measure word
explanation: With round numbers like 10, 20 or 100, put 多 before the measure word to mean 'more than': 二十多岁 is in your twenties.

examples.py: Tā èrshí duō suì.
examples.en: He's in his twenties.

examples.zh: 我们班有三十多个学生。
examples.py: Wǒmen bān yǒu sānshí duō gè xuésheng.
examples.en: There are over thirty students in our class.

title: A bit over: number + measure word + 多
explanation: With numbers 1 to 9 and units that can be split, like 块 or 小时, 多 comes after the unit: 五块多 is a bit over five yuan, 一个多小时 is over an hour.

examples.py: Zhège píngguǒ wǔ kuài duō.
examples.en: This apple is a bit over five yuan.

examples.py: Wǒ děng le yí gè duō xiǎoshí.
examples.en: I waited over an hour.
